However, the price saw renewed buoyancy in the New Year, with the LME 3-month price hitting $8,575/t at the time of writing, the highest level since 19th September last year. Investors have been markedly less gloomy in the last few weeks, with fewer bad news stories about the European economies, the release of positive US corporate earnings and jobs data and indications that credit availability in China is improving. Last month, Chinese unwrought copper and copper semis imports increased to a record high of 508,940t, up 47.7% y-o-y, and copper cathode imports increased 18.2% m-o-m to a record high of 406,937t. The increase seems to have been largely driven by the relatively low copper prices together with the SHFE/LME cash price ratio, which had widened considerably in mid-December, providing an opportune moment for restocking. Improved financing opportunities within China have also made an impact. As the chart shows, this rounds off a striking acceleration in imports in 2011 from May, giving a compound monthly growth rate of 15.4%. However, buying interest in China for cathode weakened considerably in the middle of January as consumers wound down activities ahead of the Spring Festival (22-28 January) and in response to higher LME prices, leading to a consequent contraction of the SHFE/LME price ratio. the market hold the view that current prices will dissuade Chinese buyers, and that on their return from holiday they will prefer to wait for prices to move back below $8,000/t. Spot premia on imported cathode in China declined to around $110-120/t in the week before the Spring Festival from the range of $110150/t in mid-December. LME warehouse stocks have been steadily declining since early October, when inventories were around 470,000t, and are currently at their lowest level since September 2009, at around 338,000t on 25th January. A good proportion of these stocks coming out of the warehouses are apparently moving into China, and we have seen a corresponding increase in both SHFE inventories, to around 132,000t on 20th January, and Shanghai bonded warehouse stocks, to around 300,000-320,000t by mid-January. Some tonnages from the US LME warehouses have also apparently gone to the Comex warehouses because the Comex/LME arbitrage has been open (Comex prices higher) for almost the whole of January. Comex stocks have risen over 80,000t – the highest since September 2010. Elsewhere, the European market continues to be quiet but is showing some small signs of recovering sentiment. Developments in the ongoing Eurozone crisis have been markedly less hysterical in the last few weeks compared to much of H2 2011. Where there has been bad news, such as S&P’s downgrade of the credit ratings of nine Eurozone countries and the Eurozone’s EFSF debt rescue fund, along with some more recent wobbles in Greece’s recovery plan, the markets have reacted in a more muted fashion than last year. Against this background, business in the copper cathode market continues to be sluggish but © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 16 Copper Monitor February 2012 www. crugroup.com enquiries are beginning to pick up for smaller tonnages. The premia remain unchanged from last month at around $40-50/t CIF Rotterdam. The US market remains fairly quiet but we are starting to see greater optimism in this part of the world. On 20th January, the government released figures indicating that those seeking unemployment benefits fell by 50,000 to 352,000 (the lowest level since April 2008), while healthy corporate earnings reports added to the picture of a strengthening US economy. A substantial number of LME warrant cancellations have taken place recently, particularly in port warehouses such as New Orleans, pointing to material being exported to Asia. This has prompted some tightness and fe

ars about access to physical material from end-users, supporting a rise in spot enquiries.  Semi-fabricators are cautiously optimistic, with general sentiments being that things are looking more positive.  Cathode premia have remained steady at 4.5-5.0¢/lb in the south and firmed a little to around 5.5-6.5¢/lb in the Mid-West, mainly as a result of tightness - though with some contribution from freight cost increases. 

In South America, producers reported that business is also subdued, mainly due to the summer holidays and the current scarcity of spare material, but some business was done with Chinese buyers at premia levels of $120-130/t for LME grade A cathode in the early days of the new year.  However, with the closing of the SHFE/LME arbitrage window and higher copper prices, the spot market has quietened down with markedly less interest from Asia. 

##### **Closures in aluminium industry to hit Al rod supply – Cu to benefit?** 

Aluminium substitution has long been a threat to copper demand, with aluminium rods being a viable and cheaper choice with which to replace copper rods for wire and cable manufacture.  However, aluminium producers are currently facing challenging conditions, with the industry in a situation of chronic oversupply, leading to depressed prices which are currently hovering at around $2,200/t on the LME. According to CRU’s aluminium production cost curve, around 30% of the aluminium smelting industry has costs that exceed current prices, and plant closures have begun.  ZALCO’s 224,000t/y smelter in Vlissingen shut in December after becoming bankrupt and Rio Tinto, Alcoa and Norsk Hydro have all announced plans to idle or shut capacity.  Around 20% of Chinese capacity is expected to be unused in 2012, due to high energy costs and low aluminium prices. 

Given the overall situation of oversupply we might consider that the closures will simply reduce the imbalance in the market and should not impact rod production.  However, wirerod constitutes only around 10% of refined aluminium consumption, making it harder for them to compete for material with bigger end-use sectors such as the beverage packaging and car industries.  Besides, many of the closures directly impact captive hot metal rod plants at aluminium smelters.  In the last week several wire and cable manufacturers were quoted in the press expressing their concerns, with one saying “for the last six to nine months, the rod market was tight anyway. This only adds severely to that pain.”  As a result, despite a Cu:Al price ratio reaching 4:1, supply constraints should prevent aluminium from increasing its market share in the rod sector this year.  In fact, as the wire and cable manufacturers start to find aluminium rod harder to get hold of, it may even force them to use greater quantities of copper rod as a raw material. This would exacerbate scarcity in what could be an already tight copper market in 2012.  (See our consumption trends section on pages 9-13 for more d

etails.) ##### **Mine supply in 2011 struggled; 2012 opens with smelter disruption** Copper mine supply struggled in 2011, declining 2.4% y-o-y to 15.62Mt, as many of the world’s largest mines suffered from lower production due to strikes, declining ore grades and technical issues. Of the top ten copper mines in terms of contained copper production in 2010, 7 showed lower output than the previous year and in the cases of the world’s top three mines, Escondida, Grasberg and Chuquicamata, output was significantly down y-o-y. On the positive side, Grasberg has been able to resume concentrate shipments following the end of its three month strike on 16th December and repairs to its damaged concentrates pipeline. Also, with fewer labour contracts at mines due for renegotiation this year, we see a reduced likelihood of industrial action in most of the world, with the potential exception of Zambia: In the copperbelt nation, the political and social atmosphere has become markedly more nationalistic in recent months, following the election of the po

pulist President Michael Sata. However, government intervention in the recent Kansanshi strike led to miners returning to work while negotiations over the terms of the new labour contract continued. ##### **Annual miner-smelter TC/RC negotiations – no benchmark for 2012** There is to be no set of benchmark treatment and refining charges (TC/RCs) for 2012 copper concentrate frame contracts. Instead, there have been major agreements involving three sets of numbers: $63.5/6.35¢ between Freeport McMoRan and all of its smelter customers; $60.5/6.05¢ between Anglo American and the Chinese and Indian smelters; and $60.0/6.0¢ agreed between BHPB and the Chinese and Indian smelters and also by Codelco with its Chinese customers. BHP Billiton and its major Japanese customers have been unable to reach agreement on 2012 TC/RCs and have mutually opted to cancel this year’s tonnages. Given the continued deficit seen in the concentrates market, we have no doubt that BHPB will be able to place these tonnages on the spot market, where they will most likely end up in China or India. The volumes were minimal anyway, and the Japanese smelters are currently said to be well-stocked. ##### **Prices to find support on good fundamentals** More than one market commentator has questioned whether prices currently may be too high for Chinese buyers, with one saying that “they do not like copper prices with an 8 in front”. However, the LME price passed $8,000/t in the week before the Spring Festival Holiday began and has since moved up to test $8,600/t on the day of publication. Wirerod consumption picked up in Q4, however, recording a 7.1% y-o-y increase - the highest quarterly rise of 2011. The growth was aided by the loosening of the government’s monetary policy in the latter part of the quarter, although the antiinflationary measures continue to impair the performance of the wirerod sector. Production was also boosted ahead of the Lunar New Year on 23rd January 2012. Nevertheless, the building wire market has slowed, and many wirerod manufacturers are nervous about taking large orders, fearing possible bad debts due to the impact of tight fiscal controls on property developers. However, of the 10 million units of social housing started in 2011, one third have been fully completed, one third have seen the floor structure completed, and one third have seen the basic structure completed, which should provide a tangible boost to wirerod consumption this year. On the other hand, state grid investment is only forecast to remain flat in 2012 compared to 2011. Railway investment is expected to pick up again in 2012, after a fall in 2011 due to the high speed train crash. Q4 also saw record imports of refined copper into China, although we believe that much of this buying behaviour on behalf of wirerod fabricators was simply the result of an effort to rebuild stocks, which were draw-down earlier in the year, while taking advantage of low copper prices. Q1 is always a seasonally slow period, so it will not be until Q2 that we see how strong the Chinese wirerod market will look for this year. From a new production perspective, there have been several announcements of increases to China’s wirerod production capacity. **Xinxing Copper** successfully increased its product

ion capacity of oxygenfree copper rod to 150,000t/y in late Q3.  Meanwhile, **Quanwei Copper Technology** , a subsidiary of **Hong Kong Zhangwei International** , recently began the installation of a second phase of new production lines at its facility in **Tongling** .  The company completed the first stage of copper semis processing units in 2009 and upon completion of the new expansion the factory will have capacity to produce 120,000t/y of copper wire and 30,000t/y of fine copper wire.  Construction also commenced at **Anhui Xinke New Materials** ' 150,000t/y copper rod project in **Wuhu Jiujiang Industrial Park** in December.  In the wiring harness sector, production commenced at **Delphi** 's wire harness plant outside of **Shanghai** , while **Leoni AG** announced that it is opening a plant in **Jining** in northeast China's **Shandong** province to produce wire harnesses for **General Motors** and other customers. 

##### **Q4 output down in Asia Pacific** 

Japan’s wirerod output was 173,000t, down by 9% y-o-y in Q4 2011.  Fabricators destocked as a result of the negative copper price momentum and the usual end of year seasonal effects.  They also responded to a fall in orders from cablemakers, which have been impacted by reduced power utilities spending in the wake of Japan’s nuclear power suspension.  The **Japan Electric Wire and Cable Association** said that shipments for the power utility sector were the lowest seen for over three decades in December.  We expect demand from this sector to remain weak in 2012.  Conversely, demand from the automotive sector resurged in the latter half of 2011, which concluded with December cable shipments for carmakers rising by 20.9% y-o-y. **Sumitomo Electric Industries Ltd.** will increase its exposure to the automotive industry with the construction of a new copper wirerod plant in Thailand.  The plant will add 17,000t/m of capacity to the company’s current 20,000t/m, which is split between rod mills in Japan and Indonesia. Sumitomo intends to supply copper wirerod primarily for processing into automotive wire harnesses and electric motors in order to meet growing demand from the emerging South East Asian car markets. 

South Korean and Taiwanese wirerod production amounted to 142,000t and 76,000t in Q4 respectively, down by 15% and 9% y-o-y.    The stocks to consumption ratio of Taiwanese rod mills fell from 4.0 in February to 2.2 in November, reflecting destocking activity due to the declining copper price trend.

South Korean export shipments fell by 14,500t, from Q4 2010 and by 4,800t from Q3 2011 as Chinese domestic wirerod production increased. **Taewoo Metals** , a South Korean wirerod producer, recently announced that it is increasing its wirerod production capacity by 50,000t to reach 170,000t/y with a KRW50B (approximately US$44.25M) investment into a new facility which is

expected to start operations imminently. 

##### **Little change in Europe from Q3** 

For Europe as a whole, copper wirerod production increased by 5.1% y-o-y in 2011.   However, this figure is highly skewed by exports of wirerod from Russia, which became a cost-effective way of avoiding a 10% tax on exports of copper cathode, which was introduced in November 2010. Consequently, when the influence of E&C Europe’s 24.9% y-o-y wirerod production increase is deducted from the calculation, it becomes evident that output in Western Europe in fact fell by 3.5% in the same period.  In Q4, Western European wirerod consumption maintained the low level observed in Q3, when the sector slowed following the emergence of copper price volatility and economic uncertainty surrounding news of the Eurozone debt crisis.  Consequently, provisional data suggests that Q4 production in Western Europe was down 6.3% y-o-y, with weakness felt more strongly in the south of the region, but a strongly performing automotive sector providing support nonetheless.  In December, **Glencore** acquired an estimated 40% of **Carlo Colombo** , an Italian wirerod producer with capacity of 300,000t/y (or 12% of Europe’s total) at its **Pizzeghettone** and **Pisano** mills.  The move is a vote of confidence in the attractiveness of the wirerod business in the longer run. 

##### **North America shrugs off Q3 worries** 

Wirerod production in USA was 298,000t in Q4, which is the same volume as 2010’s Q4 total.  Domestic consumption rose by 18,000t year-on-year, which was met by a reduction in exports and an equivalent increase in rod imports.  In Q4 we saw positive results from US autos, as vehicle production rose by 14% y-o-y to 2.1M units and also in construction, as US housing starts reached the highest level seen since April 2010 in November.  This implies that the industry may have reached its bottom and will continue to recover in 2012.  We anticipate that the December trade data will indicate that imports of wirerod from Russia slowed quarter-on-quarter in Q4 as was common when the trade relationship existed prior to March 2009.  Canadian wirerod output declined by 1,000t y-o-y in Q4 due to a contraction in net exports. Conversely Mexican rod production was 61,000t in Q4 2011, up from 47,000t in the previous year.  This was principally due to increased domestic consumption following strong demand from the wire and cable industry as both the automotive and power utilities sectors performed well. 

##### **Aluminium no longer a major threat to copper in 2012?** 

The use of aluminium as a conductor for insulated wire and cable and bare overhead conductor industries has been growing over the past decade, posing an ever increasing substitution threat to copper, which currently occupies the greatest share in this market.  CRU estimates that consumption of aluminium in insulated wire and cable and bare overhead conductor applications totalled 4.7 million tonnes in 2011, an impressive 16

% y-o-y rise due to booming global demand for bare overhead conductors (which are virtually 100% aluminium) and substitution gains in insulated wires and cables due to the high price and volatility of copper.  However, the prospects for aluminium appear a lot less upbeat in 2012, given indications of an impending crisis in the aluminium wirerod market. 

From a quarterly average peak of $2,600/t in Q2 2011, LME cash prices fell to $2,399/t in Q3 and then down to $2,090/t in Q4 and at present, LME prices are hovering around $2,200/t.  The main driver of the current crisis is that aluminium prices have been falling at a time when electricity prices, which account for around 33% of aluminium production costs, have been rising (except those from hydroelectric or geothermal sources) due to the general upward trend in energy inputs (oil, gas, coal).  There has also been the cost burden of investment in renewable energy sources (wind, solar, tidal) which is more expensive

than traditional energy sources and the legacy de-commissioning costs of nuclear reactors.  The need to prepare to meet more stringent guidelines on CO2 emissions is also an additional cost pressure. 

CRU estimates that at least 30% of world aluminium smelting capacity is losing money at today’s LME prices of US$2,200/t, compelling many of world’s major aluminium producers to announce significant permanent closures or temporary idling of their high cost plants. 

**Alcoa** , **Rio Tinto** and **Norsk Hydro** have so far announced closures while **Rio Tinto** has also been hit by technical failures and a labour dispute. **ZALCO** in the Netherlands has gone bankrupt, while **ALRO** in Romania has cut output because of electricity shortages.  All these constrain aluminium rod supply (particularly at smelters with captive hot metal casting lines) at a time when substitution pressures had favoured growing usage over copper in insulated wire and cable applications due to a current price ratio of 3.8:1.  Demand for aluminium rod for bare overhead conductor manufacture remains very strong globally so this will likely absorb the vast majority of decreasing aluminium rod supply, leaving little left over for insulated cablemakers to substitute for more expensive copper rod.  Conversion fees for aluminium wirerod have jumped to $600/t on annual contract.  So in the short term substitution pressures on copper will likely diminish due to declining aluminium rod availability.

- **Aurubis** , the German head-quartered copper smelter and products fabricator, reported it’s year-end production and financial position.  Revenues increased by 35.2% y-o-y to €13.3B and gross profits increased to €1.1B.  Revenues of the **copper products** business unit were €9.7B, an increase of 30.2% y-o-y.  This business unit produced 785,000t of copper wirerod, up by 2.5% y-o-y in 2010/11 and 197,000t of continuous cast copper shapes, down by 6.2% y-o-y in 2010/11. It also sold 202,000t of copper and copper alloy pre-rolled strip, down by 3.3% y-o-y.  The business unit also produced 40,000t of copper strips and 11,000t of drawn wires which are unchanged from last year’s levels. 

- According to **Chinese customs** figures, imports of refined copper, copper alloy and copper products reached a record high of 508,942t in December, up 18% m-o-m and 48% y-o-y.  This is the seventh consecutive month with a m-o-m increase in the level of copper imports.  The latest rise in import levels comes ahead of the week-long lunar New Year holiday at the end of January, with some of the rise in preparation for the usually seasonally stronger demand following the holiday. 

- **CommScope Inc.** announced on 12<sup>th</sup> January that it has developed a copper-alternative grounding wire designed to deter copper theft and lower maintenance costs for telecoms and data applications. By making use of copper clad steel wire which has copper metallurgically bonded to a solid steel core, this solution is more resistant to cutting and has a lower scrap value. This is seen welcome solution for the telecommunications industry as telecoms operators traditionally use copper ground wire for network grounding and bonding. With high and volatile copper prices, increasing costs and problems with theft have created major concerns for many companies. 

- It was reported on 27<sup>th</sup> December 2011 that power cable producer **Jiangsu Zhongchao Cable** plans to acquire three industry peers through a private placement. Zhongchao Cable plans to issue a maximum of 68 million shares, at no less than RMB13.43 (US$2.10) per share, in order to raise a maximum of RMB900M (US$142.M) to acquire 51% stakes in **Yufang Cable** , **Mingzhu Cable** and **Xizhou Magnet Wi

res** , and to set up an operations centre in Shanghai. According to the filing, controlling shareholder, **Jiangsu Zhongchao Group** , plans to spend between RMB100M and RMB300M (US$15.9M and US$47.6M) for the private placement. 

##### **Mine Production** 

- **Freeport-McMoRan** announced on 18<sup>th</sup> January that it had restarted concentrate shipments at the **Grasberg mine** , after a three-month long strike there ended in December.  The return of workers, however, had been delayed due to a combination of technical issues, safety fears and fresh demands for workers’ pay covering the strike period.  In early January, a gradual return of the workers was initiated with several hundred of the 8,000 workers transported to the remote mining site.  However, the return had to be halted again on 10<sup>th</sup> January, after gunmen ambushed and shot dead two contractors dead on the road to the mine.  We estimate Grasberg to have produced 422,000t of copperin-concentrate in 2011, which is a reduction of 78,000t compared to our July estimate. 

- Production was halted at **First Quantum** ’s **Kansanshi** mine, Zambia’s largest copper mine, after around 500 workers undertook strike action on 3-4<sup>th</sup> January in response to the slow pace of their contract renegotiations.  The labour force had demanded a wage increase of 20% and other benefits, but, after negotiations broke down, they raised their claim to a 100% pay rise.  The Zambian government intervened to end the stoppage and the **workers’ union** said that negotiations would continue one week later.  In 2011, the mine produced around 130,000t of copper-in-concentrate. 

- A union spokesperson said on 2<sup>nd</sup> January that a deal had been struck between the **workers’ unions** for the **Chambishi** copper mine in Zambia and Chinese-owned **NFCA Mining** .  The agreement, which entitles the workforce to a 44% pay rise, comes after several weeks of negotiation.  Production at the Chambishi mine is estimated to have totalled 43,000t of copper-in-concentrate in 2011.

- On 17<sup>th</sup> January, the **Polish government** approved a new mining tax on copper and silver, following two revisions to its original proposal, which had been drawn up by the finance ministry on 15<sup>th</sup> December 2011.  The approved tax on copper will be a maximum 1,320PLN (US$392) if the price of copper is below 15,000PLN /t (US$4,452/t) and will increase exponentially until it reaches a cap of 16,000PLN/t (US$4,749/t) if the price exceeds 46,160PLN /t (US$13,701/t).  In the original proposal, the tax cap was set at 32,000PLN (US$9,498) if the price of copper exceeded 52,000PLN (US$15,434). In response to the latest news, a union representing 5,000 of the 18,500 workers at **KGHM** , Poland’s sole copper miner, has threatened to stage a strike.  The final tax proposal is still pending

parliamentary approval. KGHM operates the **Lubin** , **Polkowice-Sieroszowice** and **Rudna** mines that combined are estimated to have produced 422,000t of copper-in-concentrate in 2011. 

- It was announced on 9<sup>th</sup> January that a new 45-month collective labour contract was settled at **Teck Resources Limited** ’s **Carmen de Andacollo** mine in Chile, replacing the previous agreement that expired on 31<sup>st</sup> December.  Carmen de Andacollo produced 65,000t of copper-in-concentrate in 2011. In related news, it was reported on 25<sup>th</sup> January, that workers at Teck’s **Quebrada Blanca** mine in Chile are likely to reject the company’s wage proposal and go on strike after the current contract expires on the 31<sup>st</sup> January. The mine produced 63,000t of EW cathode in 2011. 

- In early October, **Codelco** announced its intention to exercise an option agreement to acquire 49% of **Anglo American Sur** (AAS). **Anglo American** (AA), which has the controlling interest over AAS, subsequently refused to sell the shares to Codelco and a legal battle ensued.  The latest news is the announcement by Codelco on 10<sup>th</sup> January that it was lifting the injunction won on November 15<sup>th</sup> blocking the sale of shares in AAS.  This comes after, on 22<sup>nd</sup> December, AA filed a writ against Codelco for breach of contract, claiming that the Chilean miner invalidated the terms of the option agreement by attempting to exercise it before January 2012.  AAS’s assets include the **Los Bronces** and **El Soldado** mines and the **Chagres** smelter.  In 2011, Los Bronces and El Solado produced an estimated 200,000t and 35,000t of copper-in-concentrate, respectively.  We estimate that the Chagres smelter produced 140,000t of refined copper in 2011. 

- It was reported on 9<sup>th</sup> January that the **Australian government** ’s health and safety body, NT **WorkSafe** , has ordered mining company **OZ Minerals** to clean up a spill of copper concentrate into the Edith River. The spill was caused by a flash flood on 27<sup>th</sup> December which led to the derailment of a train carrying the material from the **Prominent Hill** mine to Darwin. It was reported that around 1,200t of the material have been washed down the river. Pollution tests confirmed that the spill did not cause chemical levels in the river to exceed safety guidelines. Under the order, OZ Mineral is only required to clean-up the site of the crash and its immediate surroundings.

These include the **Kolwezi Tailings Project,** the **Frontier** and **Lonshi** mines and related exploration interests. As part of the deal, ENRC will acquir

e **Frontier SPRL** (the former owner and operator of the Frontier mine) and **Compagnie Miniere de Skania SPRL** (the former owner and operator of the Lonshi Mine).
